slides.title: DeCAL: Towards Physically-Grounded Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Models via Contact-Aware Latent Co-Imagination
slides.highlight: DeCAL introduces a vision-language-action model with adaptive visuo-tactile fusion and latent co-imagination for contact-rich manipulation. This contributes to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception and the integration of diverse sensory inputs for complex state modeling.

card.one_liner: DeCAL is a physically-grounded VLA model improving contact-rich dexterous manipulation via adaptive visuo-tactile fusion and latent co-imagination.
card.key_idea: A Mixture-of-Transformers architecture using a contact-aware gating mechanism for tactile integration and joint visuo-tactile latent prediction to model future physical dynamics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six real-world tasks against baselines like GR00T N1.6 and InternVLA-A1, achieving a 71% average success rate.
card.limitation: Reliance on accurate tactile perception susceptible to sensor noise and a lack of fingertip force feedback during teleoperation demonstrations.

slides.title: Dex-X: Learning Visual-Tactile Dexterous Manipulation From Human Videos with Simulated Interaction
slides.tldr: LEARNING DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION FROM HUMAN VIDEOS VIA SIMULATED TACTILE COMPLETION
slides.highlight: This framework uses simulation to recover tactile information from monocular human videos, enabling the training of visual-tactile policies for contact-rich tasks with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

card.one_liner: Dex-X learns visual-tactile dexterous manipulation from human videos by using simulation as a tactile completion engine.
card.key_idea: Reconstructs human videos in simulation to generate missing tactile supervision, trains a privileged state-expert via RL, and distills it into a point-cloud-based visual-tactile policy.
card.evaluation: Tested on a 29-DoF platform across six task categories; achieved 93% real-world success on cube picking and 53% on table-cleaning.
card.limitation: Sensitive to perception errors and large geometry shifts; tactile representation is limited to per-fingertip force magnitudes.

slides.title: Compact Visuotactile World Models for Lifting: Prediction, Reward Alignment, and Force Constraints
slides.tldr: VISUOTACTILE WORLD MODELS FOR FORCE-CONSTRAINED LIFTING
slides.highlight: This research explores a compact action-conditioned world model that integrates visuotactile dynamics to improve force-budgeted success in lifting tasks.

card.one_liner: A compact visuotactile world model improves force-budgeted lifting in ID and geometry-shift MuJoCo environments.
card.key_idea: A 652,157-parameter action-conditioned world model using vision, touch, and proprioception to predict forces and height, integrated with a model-assisted selector for force-constrained control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 120 MuJoCo environments (ID, geometry, and physics OOD) using joint success (lifting within 8N budget) and action-effect MAE.
card.limitation: Performance drops under physical-parameter shifts; no physical-robot transfer or closed-loop safety guarantees were provided.

slides.title: Scene Graph-Driven Haptic Feedback for Safety Enhancement in Robotic Ophthalmic Surgery via Physically Simulated iOCT
slides.tldr: SCENE GRAPH-DRIVEN HAPTIC FEEDBACK FOR MICROSURGERY
slides.highlight: This research introduces a haptic feedback system using Scene Graphs to analyze simulated iOCT feeds, reducing needle alignment error by 14% in robotic subretinal injections.

card.one_liner: A haptic feedback system using Scene Graphs to improve precision in robotic subretinal injection surgery.
card.key_idea: Real-time Scene Graphs (SGs) translate simulated iOCT visual data into semantic states, which a rule-based engine maps to context-aware vibrotactile cues for the surgeon.
card.evaluation: User study (N=16) with a robotic phantom; results showed 14% reduced alignment error and 8% higher SUS scores (p < 0.05).
card.limitation: Small sample size, lack of tissue deformation, and reliance on simulated rather than clinical iOCT data.

slides.title: WM-Craftnet: World Synesthesia Model for Generalizable and Robust Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
slides.tldr: WORLD-MODEL-CONDITIONED FRAMEWORK FOR ROBUST DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: WM-Craftnet utilizes a World Synesthesia Model to learn latent dynamics from multimodal sensing, enhancing the robustness of dexterous in-hand manipulation. This contributes to MIMIC by providing a method for agent models to handle noisy observations and generalize across diverse objects.

card.one_liner: WM-Craftnet uses a world-model-conditioned framework to achieve robust, generalizable dexterous in-hand object rotation.
card.key_idea: A Dreamer-style recurrent state-space model learns action-conditioned latent dynamics from noisy depth, tactile, and proprioceptive data, providing a denoised geometric context for an actor-critic policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation and real-robot tests on multiple objects (including unseen ones) across x, y, z axes; outperformed baselines in success rate and rotation speed.
card.limitation: Current tasks are short-horizon, and recovery from severe perturbations remains limited when objects exceed the hand workspace or drift.

slides.title: M3-Tele: A Unified Multimodal Teleoperational Framework for Compliant Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL TELEOPERATION FRAMEWORK FOR MOBILE MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing aligned visual, tactile, force, and proprioceptive observations, supporting the HyECHO goal of multimodal social perception and state observation.

card.one_liner: M3-Tele is a multimodal teleoperation framework for compliant, whole-body mobile manipulation in contact-rich tasks.
card.key_idea: Combines task-space admittance control for force adaptation, QP-based whole-body inverse kinematics for base-arm coordination, and optical tactile feedback for adaptive gripper control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via user studies on four tasks (wiping, drawer opening, etc.) and Diffusion Policy learning; force tracking error dropped from 4.132N to 0.346N.

slides.title: BIFTA: Brain-Inspired Few-Shot Tactile Adaptation for Unknown Sensors
slides.highlight: The BIFTA framework enables data-efficient adaptation of tactile models to unknown sensors, supporting the development of embodied interaction across heterogeneous hardware for RwB.

card.one_liner: BIFTA enables frozen tactile foundation models to rapidly adapt to unknown sensors using few labeled examples.
card.key_idea: Combines dual-view statistical memory, support-conditioned spectral graphs to repair feature neighborhoods, and uncertainty-gated recurrent propagation to integrate reliable cross-query evidence without updating the encoder.
card.evaluation: Tested on SITR, TacVerse Shape, and TacQuad datasets using TVL and Sparsh backbones. BIFTA significantly outperformed baselines in classification and identity ranking.

slides.title: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Contact-Rich Assembly via Proprioception-Anchored Cross-Modal Pretraining
slides.highlight: The PACE encoder improves sim-to-real transfer in contact-rich assembly by aligning visual and force/torque representations with proprioceptive state transitions. This supports the MOSAIC goal of integrating ego-exo views and physics-based force measurements for skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: PACE enables zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for contact-rich assembly by anchoring visual and force representations to proprioception.
card.key_idea: A cross-modal encoder uses zero-sum temporal kernels and a cycle-consistency objective to predict proprioceptive state transitions, suppressing domain-specific noise while retaining motion cues.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four assembly tasks (Factory and AutoMate benchmarks); achieved 93.3% average real-world success rate with only a 2.7pp sim-to-real drop.
